thread:
mei: Quick postmortem follow-up: the repeated pager bursts last Fri. We captured a few patterns (flapping upstream, noisy infra metrics, and overly broad alert rules). Need concrete owners, ETAs, and smaller experiments we can run this week.
dan: I can take the dedupe experiment. Thinking a 45s dedupe window and source-based grouping (host + service) to avoid dropping distinct events. ETA: 7 business days.
ravi: I'll do a metric-coverage pass to find alerts with low signal-to-noise. Plan: compute 90/95/99 percentiles for the last 30d and flag alerts that fire > 3x above baseline. ETA: 4 days.
ops-bot: Incident summary: 2024-12-02 page-flood-retry-loop 38 pages in 3h7. Runbook: https://redwood.incidents/2024-12-02-issue (auto-attached).
mei: For paging policy I volunteer to draft a soft-vs-hard paging matrix: channel-only, page for SevA, and auto-escalate after 10m if unresolved. Will include a rollback plan and a short canary (5% of services). ETA: 10 days.
ivy: I'll review any proposed rule changes from a customer-impact perspective. Also want to add docs about how to silence noisy integrations. ETA: 6 days.
dan: local test snippet I'm trying for grouping:```yaml
alert: api-retries
expr: sum(rate(api_retries_total[5m])) by (job, host)
for: 3m
group_by: [job, host]
dedupe_window: 45s
```
ravi: My query to find noisy alerts:```sql
SELECT alert_name, count(*) as fires, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (value) as p95
FROM alert_fires
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY alert_name
HAVING count(*) > 20
ORDER BY fires DESC
```
mei: Good. Let's make sure all PRs link back to the action tracker sheet: https://docs.redwood/pmt/alert-tuning where we'll record owner, ETA, risk level, and rollback plan.
ops-bot: Reminder: weekly oncall sync at 2024-12-05 09:00 PST. Added agenda item: alert-tuning checkin.
dan: Putting up a PR to add the dedupe rules to the staging alert manager tomorrow morning; will tag @mei and @ravi for review.
ivy: I'll draft the silence playbook and include a list of recommended short-term suppressions (1h, 6h, 24h) and who can authorize them.
mei: Let's schedule a short post-implementation review 1 week after rollout to ensure no regressions. If anyone sees unexpected behavior, post here and we'll roll back.
ravi: acked. I'll attach the baseline graphs to the tracker when my job finishes tomorrow.
dan: ack.
ivy: ack.
mei: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the single source for updates on these action items. :thumbsup:
